curation.lead:
Red Planet Ventures is a set of three Texas limited liability companies—Red Planet Ventures I, II, and III—formed on February 25, 2025, at the shared mailing address used by Elon Musk’s family office and more than fifteen other Musk-controlled entities [Finding #5909]. The three LLCs were filed by Jared Birchall, Musk’s longtime money manager, on the same day he signed the X.AI Corp Form D for a business combination filing with the SEC, as analysis of SEC filings indicates [Finding #5910]. Their sequential Texas Secretary of State file numbers (0805920034, 0805920052, 0805920058) confirm a single batch filing [Finding #5886].

The formation date falls exactly 36 days into Musk’s tenure as head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which began January 20, 2025, according to analysis of formation timing [Finding #5910]. Despite their venture-fund architecture, as of March 2026—thirteen months after formation—the entities show no SEC filings, no Legal Entity Identifiers, no officers on record, no website, no known investors, and no disclosed investments, as a synthesis of records indicates [Finding #6239]. They are, in effect, dormant shelf companies whose Mars-themed naming echoes Musk’s branding pattern across his corporate network.

Red Planet Ventures is structurally significant not for what it has done but for what it reveals about the infrastructure-creation habits of the Musk family office: pre-positioned corporate shells with investment-fund architecture, formed during a period of government service that, analysis of DOGE actions suggests, gave Musk extensive visibility into federal procurement, regulatory pipelines, and agency restructuring [Finding #5918].
curation.system_role: Red Planet Ventures represents pre-positioned venture capital infrastructure created within the Musk family office network during Musk's DOGE government advisory tenure, illustrating how corporate shell formation can precede and potentially anticipate regulatory and market shifts driven by the principal's own government access.

sections.title: Corporate Formation and Structure
sections.content:
Three Texas LLCs were filed simultaneously on February 25, 2025: Red Planet Ventures I LLC (SOS #0805920034, Taxpayer ID 32098973491), Red Planet Ventures II LLC (SOS #0805920052, Taxpayer ID 32098973384), and Red Planet Ventures III LLC (SOS #0805920058, Taxpayer ID 32098973327) [Finding #5909]. All three share the mailing address 2110 Ranch Road 620 S, Unit 341886, Lakeway, TX 78734-0277 [Finding #6228]. Their registered agent is Registered Agent Solutions Inc at 5301 Southwest Parkway Suite 400, Austin, TX 78735 [Finding #5909].

The I/II/III numbering convention mirrors standard venture capital fund architecture: Entity I typically serves as the general partner or management company, Entity II as the main limited partner fund vehicle, and Entity III as a carried interest or co-investment vehicle, according to analysis of the filing structure [Finding #6226]. This same multi-entity pattern was used in Musk’s Twitter acquisition (X Holdings I, X Holdings II, X Holdings Corp), and examination of both structures suggests a deliberate replication of proven corporate architecture [Finding #6226]. A lateral check of adjacent Texas SOS file numbers found no co-formation cluster at the same zip codes, confirming the three Red Planet entities were filed as an isolated batch [Finding #6233].

Each entity has exactly one filing with the Texas Secretary of State: the Certificate of Formation dated February 25, 2025 [Finding #6237]. No amendments, annual reports, or ownership changes have been filed in the thirteen months since formation. Texas LLC law does not require annual reports, so the absence of follow-on filings is legally unremarkable but provides no additional public data on beneficial ownership [Finding #6237].

sections.title: Musk Family Office Network
sections.content:
The PO Box used by all three Red Planet Ventures entities (Unit 341886 at 2110 Ranch Road 620 S, Lakeway, TX) is the same address used by at least fifteen other Musk-controlled entities, including Excession LLC (the Musk family office), Musk Foundation, The Foundation, and numerous operating and holding companies [Finding #5914]. A February 2026 New York Times investigation identified approximately 90 Texas companies in the Musk personal network, with Red Planet Ventures I LLC among those sharing the Lakeway PO Box [Finding #6224].

Jared Birchall is listed as manager of Red Planet Ventures I LLC per OpenCorporates records and Texas SOS filings [Finding #6224]. Birchall serves as the operational nexus of the entire Musk corporate network: he is president of The Foundation (which received $470 million from Musk Foundation in 2024), Corporate Secretary of X.AI Holdings Corp, CFO of Neuralink Corporation, and head of Excession LLC, according to analysis of SEC filings [Finding #5910]. On the same day he filed the Red Planet Ventures entities, Birchall signed the X.AI Corp February 2025 Form D, indicating this was an administrative batch processing day within the family office [Finding #5910].

A separate, unrelated entity named Red Planet Ventures LLC was found in Delaware (company #7415573, incorporated April 19, 2023), with a different registered agent (A Registered Agent Inc, Dover, DE) and no connection to the Musk network [Finding #6232]. The Texas entities have no presence in Delaware or Nevada corporate registries [Finding #6225].

sections.title: Regulatory and Financial Footprint
sections.content:
Thirteen months after formation, Red Planet Ventures has left no trace in federal financial or regulatory systems. SEC EDGAR returns zero results for "Red Planet Ventures" in both full-text and company-name searches [Finding #6212] [Finding #6211] [Finding #6231]. No Form D filings exist for any of the three entities, meaning either no securities offering has occurred, the entities are structured to avoid Regulation D notice requirements, or required filings have not been made [Finding #5910]. Birchall’s simultaneous filing of the X.AI Corp Form D on the same day as the Red Planet formation demonstrates that the family office was actively making SEC filings during this period, making the Red Planet absence a deliberate choice rather than an oversight [Finding #5910].

No Legal Entity Identifier has been registered with GLEIF for any of the three LLCs [Finding #6217]. LEI registration is typically required for entities participating in regulated financial markets such as derivatives trading or securities lending, and its absence is consistent with pre-operational entities or entities operating outside those markets. No federal litigation involving Red Planet Ventures as a named party was found in CourtListener [Finding #6219]. Two Musk-linked cases were found using the shared PO Box address—Tarantino v. Musk (1:25-cv-00335, W.D. Texas) and Sigmon v. Musk (2:23-cv-00757, S.D. West Virginia)—but neither names the Red Planet entities [Finding #6220].

The domain redplanetventures.com is parked and listed for sale on Afternic, a domain marketplace [Finding #6221]. No branding, team listing, investment thesis, or portfolio disclosure exists online. GDELT news monitoring returned zero relevant coverage, and the entities do not appear in ICIJ offshore leak databases [Finding #6222] [Finding #6223].

sections.title: DOGE Timing and Potential Positioning
sections.content:
The formation of Red Planet Ventures 36 days into Musk’s DOGE tenure is the central question surrounding these entities [Finding #5910]. Between January 20, 2025 (DOGE start) and February 25, 2025 (RPV formation), DOGE was engaged in aggressive government restructuring: USAID was dismantled, HHS was reorganized, the Education Department was targeted for downsizing, and 2,300 GSA contracts were terminated on February 24 alone—the day before the Red Planet filing [Finding #5918]. A Public Citizen analysis found that DOGE targeted agencies where Musk had a direct business interest in over 70 percent of cases [Finding #5918].

The three-fund architecture suggests preparation for a venture capital deployment across multiple investment vintages [Finding #6226]. Sectors undergoing deregulation during this period—healthcare, finance, energy, digital assets, and environmental regulation—are precisely the sectors where new investment opportunities would emerge from reduced regulatory barriers [Finding #5918]. The inference that Red Planet Ventures was positioned to invest in sectors benefiting from DOGE deregulation remains unconfirmed: no investments, investors, or capital commitments have been publicly documented [Finding #6239].

The synthesis of available evidence characterizes Red Planet Ventures I/II/III as dormant shelf LLCs: Musk/Birchall fund architecture created during DOGE tenure with zero observable activity in thirteen months [Finding #6239]. This is consistent with three interpretations: the entities were parked for future use after Musk’s government service ended, they were created but subsequently abandoned, or they are operating through channels that do not produce public filings. The last possibility—a fund structure avoiding all SEC notice requirements—would be unusual for entities of this apparent scale and sophistication [Finding #6239].

open_questions: What is the intended investment thesis for the three Red Planet Ventures funds, and does it overlap with sectors where DOGE reduced regulatory capacity during Musk's government service?
Who are the limited partners, if any, committed to the Red Planet Ventures fund vehicles, and do they include individuals or entities that benefited from DOGE-driven policy changes?

Why has no SEC Form D been filed for any Red Planet entity thirteen months after formation, when Birchall filed the X.AI Corp Form D on the same day as the Red Planet batch filing -- does this indicate a deliberate exemption strategy or simply that no capital has been raised?

Has any capital been deployed through the Red Planet entities via informal or intra-network channels (e.g., loans, convertible notes, or inter-entity transfers within the Excession family office structure) that would not trigger public filing requirements?

Do the Red Planet Ventures entities have any relationship to SpaceX's Mars colonization plans, given the naming convention, or is the Mars branding purely thematic -- following the pattern of Europa 100 (Jupiter moon) and other celestial-themed Musk entities?
